rules.title: San Francisco ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices using nonpublic competitor data
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use qualifying algorithmic devices that calculate nonpublic competitor information to advise on rent or occupancy. Tenants may sue for damages, injunctive relief and civil penalties. Each month of use for each affected unit may be a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each unit-month may be a separate violation

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords using qualifying algorithmic devices; the alert states no size or age limits.

rules.quoted_span: The ordinance prohibits landlords from using qualifying algorithmic devices that calculate nonpublic competitor information to advise on rent or occupancy.
rules.review_note: Secondary source (law-firm alert); verify against the ordinance text.

rules.title: San Diego ban on algorithmic rent-setting and private remedy
rules.requirement: Prohibits improper use of algorithmic rent-setting products such as RealPage. Tenants may sue for damages, injunctive relief and penalties. Each month and each affected rental property may be a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and affected property may be a separate violation

coverage.summary: Coverage limits not stated in the alert.

rules.quoted_span: San Diego similarly authorizes tenant suits for damages, injunctive relief and penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, with each month and affected rental property potentially constituting a separate violation.
rules.review_note: Secondary source; the alert describes the prohibition only as 'similar' to San Francisco's.

rules.title: Berkeley ban on coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Prohibits coordinated pricing algorithms in rent setting. Recurring unit/month violations and private remedies are available. A federal challenge by RealPage was voluntarily dismissed with prejudice on Jan. 14, 2026.
rules.key_value: Recurring per-unit, per-month violations; dollar penalty not stated in the alert

coverage.summary: Coverage limits not stated in the alert.

rules.effective_date_note: The alert says 'effective January 2026' with no day. The ordinance's own text may give a different date.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits coordinated pricing algorithms; recurring unit/month violations and private remedies, previously at issue in RealPage, Inc. v. City of Berkeley et al., (N.D. Cal.) (voluntarily dismissed with prejudice Jan. 14, 2026).
rules.conflict_note: This secondary source gives only a month (January 2026). The effective date may differ from the ordinance's own text; check the primary ordinance.
rules.review_note: Secondary source; no section-level citation or penalty amount is given.

rules.title: Santa Ana ordinance against automated rent price-fixing
rules.requirement: Prohibits specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing. Tenants may bring private claims. Penalties accrue per violation and per month.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation and per month

coverage.summary: Coverage limits not stated in the alert.

rules.quoted_span: Ordinance NS-3090 prohibits specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing; private tenant claims and up to $1,000 per violation and per month.
rules.review_note: The municipal code section is not given; the alert cites only the ordinance number.

rules.title: Philadelphia ban on algorithmic rent coordination (RealPage-type services)
rules.requirement: Prohibits subscribing to and using algorithmic rent services such as RealPage. An aggrieved person may elect statutory damages or treble actual damages, plus equitable relief, interest and attorney fees and costs.
rules.key_value: $2,000 per violation or treble actual damages, plus fees

coverage.summary: Coverage limits not stated in the alert.

rules.quoted_span: Philadelphia’s ordinance permits an aggrieved person to elect statutory damages of $2,000 per violation or treble actual damages, together with equitable relief, interest and attorney fees and costs.

rules.title: Minneapolis ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data
rules.requirement: Prohibits algorithmic devices that use nonpublic competitor data to advise on vacancy or rental rates. Tenants may pursue civil actions.

coverage.summary: Coverage limits not stated in the alert.

rules.quoted_span: Prohibits algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data to advise on vacancy or rental rates; tenants may pursue civil actions.
rules.review_note: Secondary source; no penalty amount stated.

rules.title: Providence ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.requirement: Bans algorithmic rent-setting devices and dynamic pricing systems used to coordinate rental prices. The city solicitor may bring enforcement actions. Civil penalties, costs and attorney fees are available in a successful action.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $500 per day per violation, plus costs and attorney fees

coverage.summary: Coverage limits not stated in the alert.

citation_aliases: Providence Code of Ordinances ch. 13, art. X, §§ 13-69–13-73
rules.quoted_span: The ordinance authorizes the city solicitor to bring enforcement actions and provides for civil penalties of up to $500 per day per violation, as well as costs and attorney fees in a successful enforcement action.

rules.title: Jersey City ban on algorithmic rent coordination services
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic rent coordination services. The ordinance has both public and private enforcement.

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords; no size or age limits stated in the alert.

rules.quoted_span: Prohibits a landlord’s use of algorithmic rent coordination services; includes public and private enforcement; fines up to $2,000 per day.

rules.title: Hoboken ban on software and data-sharing platforms used to coordinate rents
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy.

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords; no limits stated in the alert.

citation_aliases: Hoboken City Code ch. 158, Art. II
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits landlords from using software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy.
rules.review_note: Secondary source; the citation form follows the alert.

rules.title: Seattle ban on algorithmic coordinating services
rules.requirement: Expressly prohibits specified algorithmic coordinating services in multifamily rental housing. Penalties apply per violation.

coverage.summary: Coverage limits not stated in the alert.

rules.quoted_span: Seattle’s ordinance expressly prohibits specified algorithmic coordinating services and provides penalties of up to $7,500 per violation.

rules.title: King County algorithmic rent-coordination law: renter remedies
rules.requirement: Injured renters may seek actual damages, per-violation damages and attorney fees under the county's algorithmic rent-coordination law.
rules.key_value: Up to $7,500 per violation, plus actual damages and attorney fees

coverage.summary: Coverage limits not stated in the alert.

rules.quoted_span: Injured renters may seek actual damages, up to $7,500 per violation and attorney fees.
rules.review_note: The alert describes only remedies, not the prohibited conduct.

rules.title: Spokane ban on purchasing algorithmic coordinating services
rules.requirement: Landlords may not purchase algorithmic coordinating services. City enforcement includes civil penalties.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $5,000 per violation

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords; no other limits stated in the alert.

rules.quoted_span: Prohibits landlords from purchasing algorithmic coordinating services; city enforcement includes civil penalties of up to $5,000 per violation.

rules.title: Portland ban on algorithm-assisted rental price coordination
rules.requirement: Prohibits algorithm-assisted rental price coordination. For owners of 16 or more units, private remedies include the greater of treble damages or a per-violation amount.
rules.key_value: Greater of treble damages or $1,000 per violation (owners of 16+ units)

coverage.landlord_size_condition: The private remedies described apply to owners of 16 or more units.
coverage.summary: The prohibition applies generally; the alert ties the private remedies to owners of 16 or more units.

rules.quoted_span: Prohibits algorithm-assisted rental price coordination; for owners of 16 or more units, private remedies include the greater of treble damages or $1,000 per violation.
rules.review_note: The alert does not say whether the prohibition itself is limited to 16+ unit owners.

rules.title: Rockville ban on algorithmic devices and shared competitor information in setting rent
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic devices and shared competitor information to set rent, fees, or other rental terms.

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords; no limits stated in the alert.

rules.effective_date_note: Enacted; takes effect after the query date.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits landlords from using algorithmic devices and shared competitor information to set rent, fees, or other rental terms.

no_rule_findings.jurisdiction: Montgomery County, MD; Evanston, IL; Rhode Island
no_rule_findings.finding: Other algorithmic rent-setting regulations in Montgomery County (MD), Evanston (IL) and Rhode Island are described as pending, with no bill numbers or details given.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: Many other municipal regulations remain pending, including in Montgomery County, Maryland; Evanston, Illinois; and Rhode Island.

result.doc_summary: An August 21, 2026 Morgan Lewis alert on follow-on litigation under local algorithmic rent-pricing laws. Its table lists 14 city and county ordinances, with effective dates (mostly month-only), principal features and penalties. These include Berkeley ch. 13.63 and Jersey City § 218-12 (the manifest jurisdictions), San Francisco, San Diego, Santa Ana, Philadelphia, Minneapolis, Providence, Hoboken, Seattle, King County, Spokane, Portland, and Rockville (effective Jan. 1, 2027). Other bills in Montgomery County, Evanston and Rhode Island are pending. The document covers only algorithmic rent-setting.
